articles.title: IIT Bombay Director Signs 18-Point Charter, Apologises Amid Protests Over Student's Death
articles.excerpt: After a three-day sit-in over Sahil Wakode's death, Director Shireesh Kedare agreed to an independent probe and institutional reforms; the institute denied rumors of his resignation.
articles.nri_angle: IIT Bombay is the alma mater of tens of thousands of Indian-origin engineers in the US — its governance, campus culture and handling of caste and mental-health issues are personal to the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cricket Frenzy Grips Indian and Pakistani Expatriates Across the Gulf
articles.excerpt: From Friday-morning games on Riyadh's open grounds to crowded restaurants during India-Pakistan clashes, cricket remains the cultural lifeline of South Asian expatriates — and Saudi Arabia is building a sporting future around it.
articles.image_caption: Sharjah Cricket Stadium, a popular venue for matches drawing large South Asian expatriate crowds in the Gulf. Cricket frenzy is gripping Indian and Pakistani expatriates across the Gulf.
articles.nri_angle: For millions of Indian and Pakistani workers in the Gulf, cricket is home in portable form — and Saudi Arabia's cricket push could soon give their children a national team of their own.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-American Conservatives Face Racial Gatekeeping From the MAGA Fringe
articles.excerpt: A Times of India report and U.S. coverage document racially charged attacks on Indian-American conservatives — from Ramaswamy's Ohio bid to Nikki Haley and JD Vance's family — even as immigration enforcement tightens around the community.
articles.image_caption: The U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C. Indian-American conservatives say they face racial gatekeeping from parts of the MAGA movement.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-Americans across party lines are learning that political alignment does not shield them from racial gatekeeping — while immigration enforcement tightens around the community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: JioHotstar Goes Global: Ambani Targets Diaspora in UK, Canada, Singapore
articles.excerpt: JioHotstar replaces Hotstar in Britain, Canada and Singapore with 160,000+ hours of content across 12 languages — but no live sports at launch, and pricing runs about ten times Indian plans.
articles.image_caption: Mukesh Ambani's JioHotstar is expanding beyond India to target the diaspora in the UK, Canada and Singapore.
articles.nri_angle: JioHotstar's first overseas launch puts 160,000+ hours of Indian content in 12 languages directly in front of diaspora households in the UK, Canada and Singapore.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: After Years in America, an NRI Came Home — and Felt He Didn't Belong
articles.excerpt: NDTV reported the account of an NRI who moved back after years in the United States and now describes loneliness and disconnection: "I feel like I don't belong here." The story reflects a wider, often unspoken strain among returning Indians.
articles.image_caption: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport in Mumbai. After years in America, one NRI came home — and found he no longer felt he belonged.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs weighing a return, this story underscores that repatriation is an emotional transition as much as a logistical one — belonging must be rebuilt, not just revisited.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ChatGPT Helps Stranger Reunite Lost Punjab Elder With Family 1,200 Km Away
articles.excerpt: Chaman Lal, an elderly Ludhiana man with memory issues, vanished during an Amritsar pilgrimage and surfaced in Gaya, Bihar — until a stranger used ChatGPT to trace his village and escorted him home.
articles.image_caption: Gaya Junction railway station in Bihar. The missing elder surfaced in Gaya, roughly 1,200 km from his home in Ludhiana, before a local resident helped trace his family.
articles.nri_angle: Punjabi diaspora families, who manage ageing parents' care from abroad, share the specific anxiety of an elderly relative wandering off — making this both a cautionary tale and a reassurance about strangers' kindness.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mandaviya Joins Indian Diaspora Cycle Ride to Cheer Asian Games Athletes
articles.excerpt: Union Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya cycled alongside members of the Indian community in Nagoya on Sunday as the diaspora rallied behind India's 500-strong contingent at the 20th Asian Games.
articles.image_caption: Union Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya joined the Indian diaspora in Nagoya for a Sundays on Cycle event on September 20, 2026. The community ride was organised to cheer for Indias contingent at the 20th Asian Games.
articles.nri_angle: The Nagoya ride showed the Indian diaspora in Japan turning out as volunteers and cheerleaders for the country's athletes on one of Asian sport's biggest stages.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kerala CM Satheesan Meets Jaishankar in Delhi, Flags NRI Welfare Priorities
articles.excerpt: V.D. Satheesan's meeting with the External Affairs Minister focused on consular assistance and grievance redressal for Non-Resident Keralites — his first major diaspora outreach as the state's new chief minister.
articles.image_caption: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar (left) with Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan. The two leaders met in New Delhi on Saturday to discuss welfare measures for the Non-Resident Keralite community.
articles.nri_angle: The meeting puts Pravasi welfare at the center of the new Kerala government's agenda, with consular help and grievance redressal for Keralites abroad now a direct CM-to-EAM channel.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: London NRI With Rs 38 Crore Asks: Is FatFIRE Realistic in a Tier-1 Indian City?
articles.excerpt: A London-based NRI's viral Reddit question about retiring early in India has reignited the debate over what financial independence really costs in cities like Bengaluru — and whether even a Rs 38 crore corpus is enough.
articles.image_caption: A hand stacks coins against a backdrop of stock market charts. The article examines whether a Rs 38 crore corpus is enough for FatFIRE in a Tier-1 Indian city like Bengaluru.
articles.nri_angle: The story captures the reverse-migration dilemma facing wealthy NRIs: whether a large foreign-earned corpus buys genuine financial independence back home once Bengaluru's real costs, taxes and healthcare risks are factored in.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Aadhaar for NRIs and OCI Holders: Current Rules and UIDAI’s Global Expansion Plan
articles.excerpt: As UIDAI works to take Aadhaar international, here are the rules that apply today: NRIs with Indian passports can apply on arrival but must visit India in person; OCI holders face a 182-day stay requirement.
articles.image_caption: An Aadhaar Seva Kendra enrolment centre. UIDAI is building a legal framework to let NRIs and OCI cardholders enrol without the current India-stay requirements.
articles.nri_angle: The rules split the 36-million-strong diaspora sharply: NRIs can enrol on arrival in India, but OCI holders face a 182-day stay requirement — the exact condition UIDAI’s planned liberalization would remove.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Asia Society Texas Brings Diwali Lights Back to Houston on October 18
articles.excerpt: The free, family-friendly festival of lights returns to the Texas Center in the Museum District on October 18, with food, fashion, crafts and a Ramayana performance — three weeks before Lakshmi Puja.
articles.image_caption: Diwali lights. The Asia Society Texas festival returns to Houston on October 18.
articles.nri_angle: Houston’s large Indian-American community gets one of its earliest Diwali-season celebrations of 2026 at Asia Society Texas’s free “Diwali Lights!” festival on October 18.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Oracle's Offices to a Karur Kiosk: Falooda Brand Hits Rs 9 Crore
articles.excerpt: Pradeep Kannan walked away from a Rs 1-lakh-a-month operations role at Oracle in 2019 to open a 10×10-foot falooda kiosk in his hometown. Seven years on, The Falooda Shop has 18+ outlets across India and Dubai and revenue above Rs 9 crore.
articles.image_caption: This image from StartupPedia illustrates the falooda entrepreneur story. Founder Pradeep Kannan left Oracle to sell falooda, and the brand now makes Rs 9 crore.
articles.nri_angle: The brand's Dubai outlet and franchise model make it directly relevant to Gulf-based NRIs, both as customers and potential franchise investors, as Kannan eyes global expansion.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SpaceX's Record IPO Let a 14-Year Employee Fund a Year of Dreams
articles.excerpt: After SpaceX's June 12 debut minted new millionaires, Brian Aggrey and Phoebe Novack quit their jobs and set a $25,000-a-month budget for 365 days of chasing everything from acting school to sculpture — an experiment they call their "Year of Freak."
articles.image_caption: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket with a Dragon capsule rolls out to the launch pad. The company's record IPO has put the spotlight on a 14-year employee funding a year of dreams.
articles.nri_angle: The couple has no stated Indian connection, but their equity windfall mirrors the options-driven mobility that drew generations of Indian engineers to Silicon Valley — and SpaceX's IPO turned that possibility into real capital for employees across the org chart.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IIT Madras Students' Crewless Vessel Wins Global Njord Challenge in Norway
articles.excerpt: Team Aritra beat 22 teams from nine countries at the autonomous ship competition in Trondheim, building on its 2023 podium finish.
articles.image_caption: IIT Madras Director Prof. V. Kamakoti with members of Team Aritra and their autonomous surface vessel. The ocean engineering students won the 2026 Njord Challenge in Trondheim, Norway, beating 22 teams from nine countries.
articles.nri_angle: IIT Madras students beat 22 teams from nine countries in marine robotics, another marker of Indian engineering talent winning on the world stage.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Krishnamoorthi Breaks With Indian-American Democrats on Russia Sanctions Vote
articles.excerpt: The Illinois Democrat was the sole Indian-origin House member to back the Graham sanctions bill carrying 100% tariff authority on Russian oil buyers including India.
articles.image_caption: U.S. Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi. The Illinois congressman broke with fellow Indian-American Democrats on a Russia sanctions vote.
articles.nri_angle: Krishnamoorthi's vote puts a senior Indian-American lawmaker on the opposite side of a bill that could hit India with 100% tariffs over Russian oil — a fault line the diaspora will debate.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Turns to Diaspora in Nagoya as Asian Games Accommodation Crisis Deepens
articles.excerpt: With athletes evacuated from flooded container rooms and India's shooting team left waiting until 3 a.m., some 2,000 Indians in Nagoya stand ready to open their homes.
articles.image_caption: Nagoya at night, host city of the 2026 Asian Games. The city is facing an accommodation crunch that has pushed India to lean on its diaspora.
articles.nri_angle: The Indian diaspora in Japan is literally opening its homes to athletes, turning a host-organiser failure into a showcase of community mobilization.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Indian-Origin Researchers Used Claude to Break Into OpenAI in 72 Hours
articles.excerpt: Harsh Jaiswal, Mohan Pedhapati and Rahul Maini chained two vulnerabilities from OpenAI's public forum to employee accounts, then disclosed it for a $6,500 bounty.
articles.image_caption: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman at a public appearance. The attempted breach targeted OpenAI internal systems, according to a new cybersecurity report.
articles.nri_angle: Three Indian-origin security researchers delivered the most embarrassing demonstration yet of AI-era vulnerability — breaking into OpenAI with a rival's model in 72 hours.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Harvard to Offer Executive Education Courses in Hyderabad from December
articles.excerpt: Telangana CM A. Revanth Reddy announced Thursday that Harvard executive education programmes will launch in Hyderabad in December 2026, with MIT and Purdue offshore campuses also in the works as the state pushes to become a global knowledge hub.
articles.image_caption: A Telangana government delegation poses with Harvard representatives in Hyderabad. Harvard will offer executive education courses in Hyderabad starting December.
articles.nri_angle: Harvard executive courses in Hyderabad give diaspora professionals a mid-career credential from a globally recognised brand without leaving India, while dual-degree and research partnerships could pull diaspora academics into Hyderabad's institutions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Edmonton South Asians finalize plans with city for central Diwali festival
articles.excerpt: After October 2025 Diwali fireworks sparked fires and a wave of hate, South Asian leaders and the City of Edmonton are finalizing a Canada Day-style central celebration at Mill Woods Park, with permits pending and details expected within weeks.
articles.image_caption: Spectators watch a fireworks display light up the night sky. Edmonton community leaders want a professionally run central Diwali fireworks show at Mill Woods Park to replace the backyard displays that sparked fires last October.
articles.nri_angle: Edmonton's South Asian leaders are converting a crisis — Diwali 2025 fireworks fires and the hate that followed — into civic recognition by co-building a city-partnered, Canada Day-style Diwali festival open to all.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Canberra University's T20 Cricket Challenge Opens Study-Play Pathway for Indian Teens
articles.excerpt: The third University of Canberra Cricket Challenge wrapped up in Bengaluru on September 4, drawing more than 300 young athletes from across India. Indian school teams now head to Canberra for the next leg later this month.
articles.image_caption: A youth cricket team in University of Canberra jerseys poses for a team photo in front of UC, Cricket ACT Australia and Jain International Residential School banners. The photo was taken during the third UC Cricket Challenge in Bengaluru, held August 30 to September 4, which brought more than 300 young cricketers from across India to compete and attend study-in-Australia workshops.
articles.nri_angle: The tournament gives Indian families a low-pressure introduction to an Australian university and offers a credible 'study and play' route for cricket-obsessed students to pair an Australian degree with elite training.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'I'm staying, so is the curry': Krishnamoorthi hits back at 'go home' jibe
articles.excerpt: U.S. Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi answered Palm Bay councilman Chandler Langevin's 'take your curry and go home' post by calling America his home and refusing to let anyone decide who belongs in the country.
articles.image_caption: U.S. Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi at an event in Washington, D.C. The Illinois Democrat told Palm Bay councilman Chandler Langevin this week: "I am staying. So is the curry. America is my home."
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-origin U.S. congressman publicly rejects a Florida councilman's 'go home' taunt, turning a recurring anti-Indian attack into a defense of who belongs in America.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tata Sons Board Reinstates Chandrasekaran for Five Years; Trusts Call Move Illegal
articles.excerpt: The board reversed Chandrasekaran's August decision to step down, but controlling shareholder Tata Trusts says the majority vote was a "legal nullity" — and the RBI has revived the long-dodged listing question.
articles.image_caption: File photo of N. Chandrasekaran, executive chairman of Tata Sons. On September 17, 2026, the Tata Sons board voted to reappoint him for a third five-year term, a move Tata Trusts called a legal nullity.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora investors, the stakes are direct: TCS is a top Indian-American portfolio holding and a Tata Sons listing could be one of the largest IPOs in Indian history.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Firm Accused of Firing Entire 80-Member Indian Support Team on 5-Minute Call
articles.excerpt: According to an employee's viral account, a US-based company — described in reports as a bank — dismissed its whole Indian customer service team in a single brief Google Meet call. The allegation has not been independently verified.
articles.image_caption: A customer service call center in India. A US-based company was accused of firing its entire 80-member Indian support team during a five-minute Google Meet call, in an account that has not been independently verified.
articles.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian professionals staff customer service and back-office operations for US companies remotely, and an alleged five-minute dismissal of an entire 80-person team underscores how precarious that arrangement can be.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Supreme Court Demands Answers on 34 Unnatural Deaths in Manipur Relief Camps
articles.excerpt: A bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant ordered Manipur's chief secretary to file an affidavit explaining why post-mortems were conducted in only 20 cases and why bereaved families received as little as Rs 20,000 in compensation.
articles.image_caption: A photograph from the Supreme Court Observer's coverage of the Manipur hearing. On September 17, the Supreme Court expressed shock over 34 unnatural deaths in relief camps and directed the state's chief secretary to file an affidavit accounting for each one.
articles.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora — including human-rights advocates and community groups that have followed Manipur closely since 2023 — the Supreme Court's intervention signals that accountability for the displaced extends beyond the violence itself to the conditions in which survivors are living and dying.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Hyderabad Man Dies in US 17 Days After Wedding; Family Seeks Jaishankar's Help
articles.excerpt: Mohammed Jaber Hussain, 27, died in Lowell, Massachusetts, on September 14. His family, citing financial hardship, has appealed to EAM S. Jaishankar and Hyderabad MP Asaduddin Owaisi for help bringing his body home.
articles.nri_angle: A Hyderabad family's sudden loss in Massachusetts exposes the financial and bureaucratic burden diaspora families face repatriating loved ones from the US, and their routine reliance on EAM intervention and consular coordination.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sethuraman Panchanathan Becomes First Indian American to Win NAE's Bueche Award
articles.excerpt: The former NSF director, now a University Professor of Technology and Innovation at Arizona State University, was cited for advancing translational research and U.S. science policy. He will receive the 2026 award on Oct. 4 in Washington, D.C.
articles.image_caption: Sethuraman Panchanathan. He is the first Indian American to receive the National Academy of Engineering's Arthur M. Bueche Award.
articles.nri_angle: A Chennai-born scientist who rose to lead U.S. science funding becomes the first Indian American honored by the National Academy of Engineering for shaping national science and technology policy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ahaana Krishna Marries 'Lokah' Cinematographer Nimish Ravi in Kerala Wedding
articles.excerpt: The Malayalam actor and 'Lokah' cinematographer tied the knot on September 13 in an intimate Kovalam ceremony, announcing it on Instagram with the line: 'Met you at 20, Married you at 30.'
articles.image_caption: Actress Ahaana Krishna and cinematographer Nimish Ravi in their wedding announcement photo. The couple married on September 13, 2026, at Taj Green Cove Resort in Kovalam, Kerala, announcing the news on Instagram on September 15.
articles.nri_angle: Malayalam cinema weddings command wide attention among the global Malayali diaspora, and the couple's decade-long friendship-to-marriage story has resonated across social media with fans in Kerala and abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tiny English Village Votes to 'Secede' From UK Over Asylum Centre Plan
articles.excerpt: Piddington's 285-to-26 symbolic vote to become a 'principality' is the latest flashpoint in Britain's bitter fight over where to house asylum seekers.
articles.nri_angle: For the UK's large Indian diaspora, Piddington's vote is a barometer of how heated Britain's immigration debate has become — a political climate that shapes daily life for all migrant communities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Investigators Probe Possible Intoxication in NYC Subway Deaths of Indian-Origin Woman, Friend
articles.excerpt: Malaika Chitre, 24, and Navam Kaul, 24, were struck by a No. 4 train at Lower Manhattan's Spring Street station early Sunday; law-enforcement sources say detectives are examining whether alcohol or drugs left the pair unaware of the danger.
articles.image_caption: A figure sits on a New York City subway platform as a train waits beyond the tracks. Investigators are examining whether intoxication played a role in the September 13 deaths of Malaika Chitre and Navam Kaul at the Spring Street No. 4 station.
articles.nri_angle: Two young people rooted in New Jersey's South Asian community died in a tragedy now being picked apart in the press, making careful, attributed reporting — not speculation — the standard their families and community deserve.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: GOP Nominee Bo French Faces Backlash Over Post Targeting UT Students Who Look Indian
articles.excerpt: The Republican nominee for Texas Railroad Commission drew condemnation from Senator John Cornyn, Governor Greg Abbott and Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi after portraying diverse Longhorns fans as proof Americans are being 'displaced by foreigners.'
articles.image_caption: Bo French, Republican nominee for the Texas Railroad Commission. His posts about University of Texas students drew condemnation from Senator John Cornyn and other Republicans.
articles.nri_angle: South Asian American students were the direct targets — and their representatives in Congress called the post part of a broader rise in attacks on the community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Five Ts, One Mission: New Atlanta Envoy Sumit Seth Maps India's Southeast Push
articles.excerpt: Days after taking charge as Consul General of India in Atlanta, Dr. Sumit Seth laid out his priorities — consular delivery first, then trade, technology, tourism and talent — for the Southeast's fast-growing Indian diaspora.
articles.image_caption: Dr. Sumit Seth, Consul General of India in Atlanta. He took office on August 26, 2026, and has laid out a Five Ts agenda for the Southeast.
articles.nri_angle: The Southeast's large, educated and fast-growing Indian diaspora is the direct audience — better consular service and sharper economic matchmaking affect their daily lives and businesses.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-American Congressman Suhas Subramanyam Unveils Four-Bill National Data Center Plan
articles.excerpt: The Virginia Democrat's package would make data centers pay for their own grid upgrades, set federal siting and measurement standards, and protect communities living near AI infrastructure.
articles.image_caption: Rep. Suhas Subramanyam (D-Va.). The Indian-American congressman introduced a four-bill National Data Center Plan on September 9, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American Congressman Suhas Subramanyam is driving one of Congress's most prominent efforts to regulate the AI-era data-center buildout, giving the diaspora a seat at the center of national tech-infrastructure policy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: BRICS Summit 2026: India's Global South Outreach Courted ASEAN, Africa, GCC and BIMSTEC
articles.excerpt: At the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India used its presidency to bring the chairs of ASEAN, the African Union, CELAC, the GCC and BIMSTEC into the conversation on the Global South — closing with the unanimous New Delhi Declaration.
articles.image_caption: BRICS leaders seated at the summit table in New Delhi, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the center. India used its 2026 chairmanship to court ASEAN, African, GCC and BIMSTEC leaders on the Global South agenda.
articles.nri_angle: The summit's Global South outreach to the GCC, ASEAN and Africa touches issues — remittance costs, energy security, trade flows — that directly affect millions of Indians living and working in those regions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Who Is Asha Sharma? The Wisconsin-Born Executive Who Never Made a Video Game — and Is Now Running Xbox
articles.excerpt: Seven months after Microsoft handed her the Xbox controller, the former Instacart COO is cutting thousands of jobs, cutting Game Pass prices, and telling hard truths — guided by a mantra from her immigrant upbringing: clarity is kindness.
articles.image_caption: Asha Sharma at the 2026 Xbox Showcase. She became CEO of Microsoft Gaming in February 2026, succeeding Phil Spencer.
articles.nri_angle: Sharma's rise to the top of Xbox — and the racist backlash her appointment drew despite her Wisconsin birth — captures both the ascent and the friction of Indian-American leadership in 2026.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Vinayaka Chaturthi in Tamil Nadu: fervour, creative pandals and colossal offerings mark festival
articles.excerpt: From Madurai's colossal Mukkuruni Kozhukattai to a 25-kg offering atop Tiruchirappalli's Rockfort, Tamil Nadu celebrated Vinayaka Chaturthi with devotion and spectacle as police cleared 36,000 idols statewide.
articles.image_caption: Creative Ganesha idols dressed in human attire at a Vinayaka Chaturthi celebration in Tamil Nadu. This year's festival combined religious fervour with artistic innovation and record offerings.
articles.nri_angle: Vinayaka Chaturthi is one of the most widely shared festivals among Tamil communities worldwide, and Tamil Nadu's celebrations set the template diaspora temples follow.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kashmiri Pandits mark 36th Balidan Diwas, demand genocide recognition and homeland
articles.excerpt: Displaced Kashmiri Pandits observed the 36th Balidan Diwas in Jammu on September 14, renewing long-standing demands for a genocide law and a separate homeland in the Valley under direct Union protection.
articles.image_caption: Community leaders at the Panun Kashmir Balidan Diwas 2026 observance in Jammu. Kashmiri Pandits reiterated demands for recognition of the 1990s exodus as genocide and a separate homeland.
articles.nri_angle: Kashmiri Pandit diaspora groups in the US, Europe and the Middle East keep the community's demands for justice and return on the international agenda.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
